subject: Request: data-path segregation narrative + egress proof for SOC 2 submission
messages:
From: John Ellis <john.ellis@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Request: architecture narrative + egress controls for SOC2

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As part of our SOC 2 scoping for the private deployment we planned with Redwood, our audit team has asked for a concise architecture narrative that explains how data-plane traffic is segregated from the control plane in Dedicated/Private deployments, and what egress controls you have in place (allow lists, egress proxies, DNS filtering, logging).

Specifically we need: 
- A short (1-page) narrative describing isolation guarantees between customer inference workloads and control/management planes; mention of any hardware or tenancy boundaries you rely on.
- Network diagrams that show the data-path for inference requests, KV-cache and model blobs, and where egress exits (regions/peers).
- Evidence artifacts: diagram PNGs, an egress-controls matrix (who can talk where), and an index of files (for SOC2 evidence binder).

Can you get this to us by end-of-day Friday (2026-06-18)? If there are any customer-network specifics that must be redacted, please indicate that in the index.

Thanks,
John
John Ellis
Security Program Manager, Acme Corp
john.ellis@acme-corp.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: architecture narrative + egress controls for SOC2

Kim / Marissa —

Forwarding Acme's ask. They want a compact deliverable (1-page narrative + diagrams + index) for SOC 2. Can we assemble a tight package with redactions noted and a short executive summary for their auditors?

Proposed split: 
- Marissa: canonical network diagram(s) showing control vs data plane, annotate where model artifacts and KV caches live, and show egress chokepoints. Include a lightweight legend for trust domains.
- Kimberly: assemble the egress-controls matrix, include actual ACL/sg examples (redacted CIDRs), and produce the evidence index (CSV) with notes about redactions.

Deadline: Thursday EOD internal so Naomi can review and send to Acme by Friday morning.

Action items: 
- Marissa: drop draft diagram(s) in the shared drive folder and ping me when ready.
- Kimberly: start the matrix and include references to log retention/flow-logs that demonstrate egress auditing.

I'll draft the 1-page narrative once you hand off the artifacts. Keep wording conservative and avoid exposing customer IPs.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: architecture narrative + egress controls for SOC2

Naomi / Marissa —

Uploading the first pass to the drive now. Attached artifacts (stubs below) and brief notes:

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_data_path_diagram_v2.png (PNG, annotated network diagram — customer IPs redacted)
- egress-controls-matrix-v1.xlsx (Excel, rows = destination categories, cols = allowed services, enforcement points)
- soc2_evidence_index.csv (CSV, filename, description, redaction_flag)

Notes: 
- Diagram shows separate VPCs/tenancy for customer inference workloads, a managed control-plane VPC with no direct inbound paths to customer compute, and an egress NAT/proxy cluster in the infra VPC. We call out the KV cache service (managed per-tenant namespace) and show how model blobs are pulled from the artifact store with signed URLs.
- Egress matrix includes examples for commonly allowed destinations (S3 model endpoints, KMS endpoints, telemetry endpoints). I redacted customer-specific destinations and replaced with placeholders (e.g., <ACME_S3_BUCKET>).
- Evidence index references the Flow Logs export (flow-logs-sample-2026-05.csv) and a retention policy doc (logs_retention_policy_v1.pdf) — both are referenced in the CSV, not included in this thread.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodAcmeEvidence

If this looks good I'll finish a cleaned diagram (label size reductions) and Kimberly will add the ACL snippets.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Staff Security Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: John Ellis <john.ellis@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: architecture narrative + egress controls for SOC2

John —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached are the first artifacts for your SOC 2 binder; we can iterate based on auditor feedback. Summary below and links to the drive: 

What we're providing (initial drop):
- 1-page narrative (draft in drive) describing data-plane vs control-plane segregation for Dedicated/Private deployments. Key points: logical tenancy separation, per-tenant KV namespaces, signed model artifact pulls, and an infra egress/proxy cluster that mediates external connections.
- redwood_data_path_diagram_v2.png — annotated diagram showing the inference request path, KV cache boundaries, model blob fetch path, and egress chokepoints. Customer IPs redacted; placeholders used where necessary.
- egress-controls-matrix-v1.xlsx — enforcement points (network ACLs, proxy allow-lists, egress DNS filtering), examples of allowed destination categories, and references to the logging sources that prove enforcement.
- soc2_evidence_index.csv — canonical index for the binder that lists filenames, short descriptions, and redaction flags. The index points to flow-logs extracts and retention policy docs (not attached here; available on request).

Access: artifacts are in the shared drive (link below). We've applied viewer-only permissions for Acme's security group. If you need redacted PDF exports for auditors, we can produce those and timestamp them.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodAcmeEvidence

Next steps: please confirm if the auditor needs the raw flow logs (we can provide time-windowed extracts with IPs redacted), or if the indexed evidence plus diagram and matrix is sufficient. If you want, let's schedule a 30 minute sync on Friday morning to walk the auditor through the artifacts.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
